description: A pitch glider: when the voltage at the input changes, the output slides to the new pitch over a set time and along a set curve, and a chance control sets how often it slides rather than jumping

params.text: Sets how long one slide takes, from 0.01 seconds at the left to 5 seconds at the right, spaced logarithmically so the short times are the easier to set
Sets the shape of the slide: a slow start that rushes at the end on the left, a straight line at the centre, a fast start that eases in on the right; the display reads LOG, LIN or EXP
Sets the chance that a pitch change is slid to rather than jumped to, none at the left and every one at the right, rolled afresh at each change
Sets how far the TIME input can move the glide time, from nothing at the left to the whole sweep at the right
Sets how far the CURVE input can move the curve, from nothing at the left to the whole sweep at the right
Sets how far the CHANCE input can move the glide chance, from nothing at the left to the whole sweep at the right

inputs.text: The pitch to be glided, at a volt per octave; a polyphonic cable is glided channel by channel, each channel with its own slide
Voltage over the glide curve, scaled by the amount knob for this control; at full amount 10V covers the knob's whole travel
Voltage over the glide time, scaled by the amount knob for this control; at full amount 10V covers the knob's whole travel
Voltage over the glide chance, scaled by the amount knob for this control; at full amount 10V covers the knob's whole travel

outputs.text: The glided pitch at a volt per octave, with as many channels as the input carries

notes: The display above the CURVE knob draws the shape of the slide and prints LOG, LIN or EXP under it. It follows the knob and the CURVE input together, and reads the input's first channel only.
Each main knob carries two arcs on its face: a grey one showing how far its input could push it at the amount knob's present setting, and a yellow one showing where the voltage has it now.
A change smaller than 0.01V, about a sixth of a semitone in 12 tone tuning, is not counted as a new pitch and passes through without a slide.
Bypassing the module passes the pitch input straight to the pitch output.
